record_identity.title: AI-generated bank voice recordings used in Dutch NFC-relay fraud

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Dutch AI-assisted bank-helpdesk impersonation and NFC relay fraud
incident_identity.date_basis: Banks alerted police in mid-September, an approximate start; police observed approximately three weeks of activity before arrests on 6 October.

summary: In September and early October 2026, scammers used AI-generated voice recordings purporting to be banks calling about suspicious activity. Recipients were asked to press 1 and connected to a human operator posing as a bank employee. The operator instructed them to install an application and tap a payment card against a phone to supposedly block it. Card data was relayed to accomplices withdrawing cash. Rotterdam police reported approximately 170 victims and €380,000 in losses during a three-week observation window. Two suspects were arrested on 6 October, and police disabled the servers. Public disclosure followed on 21 October.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Dutch National Police reported dozens of AI-generated voice fragments used as false bank and company messages. The calls claimed suspect transactions and prompted a transfer to a human operator using a fixed urgent script. Victims installed an NFC relay application, enabling accomplices to withdraw money. Police observed roughly 170 victims and €380,000 losses over three weeks, arrested two suspected organisers on 6 October and disabled their infrastructure. Original audio, transaction-level attribution to each generated clip, the AI model and individual case outcomes were not published. Arrests do not establish criminal guilt.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: AI-generated bank-identity and urgency cues materially started a human-operated financial solicitation based on false authority. Human operators and separate NFC relay software performed subsequent fraud actions; the record does not attribute independent criminal planning or withdrawals to autonomous agents. Later police takedown does not undo realised losses. Dutch police report card-data relay through a malicious app to accomplices making withdrawals. The relayed NFC material served payment authentication outside the legitimate cardholder–bank route. This is an attributed custody transition, not a claim that static public card identifiers alone are secret authenticators. Police reporting distinguishes synthetic voice generation, human call handling and separate card-relay and withdrawal actions; those roles do not reduce the fraud or losses.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case distinguishes a synthetic trust cue, the consequential fraudulent financial request and impaired informed choice from technical fund-transfer execution. It demonstrates a human-directed AI-mediated deception mechanism with bounded realised financial harm.
assessment_boundaries: Victim count and loss total come from police observations in a three-week window, not the entire campaign lifespan.
No direct access to audio originals, individual account records or AI generation configuration.
Arrested suspects have not been shown to have been convicted.
Bank/organisation personas were used, but the record does not establish cloning of a particular identifiable employee's natural voice.
NFC relay and ATM withdrawals were performed through separate software and human actors, not by AI agents.
The exact EUR/USD threshold conversion date and rate have not yet been audited; €380,000 is materially within the ordinary S2 range.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: False generated bank authority and urgency were consequential trust cues.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The AI-generated voice posed as genuine bank security and invented urgent danger to obtain engagement with a fraudulent channel.
Police attribute creation and use of AI-generated voice clips to criminals and distinguish the synthetic voice from the later human operator.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Recipients pressed 1 and encountered a fake bank employee, who used a fixed urgent script to seek card-blocking steps.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: AI-generated solicitation and human pressure elicited a consequential, uninformed financial action.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: A synthetic bank-security warning drew recipients into a false protective request that enabled taking their funds.
The generated trust cue and human pressure materially induced victims to perform actions they could not knowingly authorise on the real theft basis.
The call recipient was transferred to a human operator using a scripted request; the source distinguishes the human conversation from the generated initial voice.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Victims installed an app and scanned cards, relaying NFC information to accomplices making withdrawals.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The technical relay and withdrawals are distinct human/software steps following the AI-mediated deceptive economic request.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The card-scanning request concealed the actual withdrawal purpose, completing the materially AI-mediated solicitation pathway.

The malicious app relayed payment-card NFC authentication data to accomplices making withdrawals. The represented purpose was card blocking by a bank, not handing payment authority to a withdrawal operator.
Police attribute card-data relay and withdrawals to accomplices and separate relay software, rather than to the voice-generation model.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Police observed about 170 victims and €380,000 in losses during roughly three weeks.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Concrete victim and loss counts are not generic exposure estimates.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Police arrested two suspects on 6 October and took the infrastructure offline.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A subsequent external intervention does not undo the observed earlier harm.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The EU AI Act prohibits specified manipulative AI techniques meeting material distortion and significant-harm conditions. Police describe deceptive AI bank calls and monetary harm, but sufficient evidence of the responsible AI deployer and every legal applicability element is absent. This is not a legal liability determination.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: Registered binding EU AI Act Article 5(1)(a), consolidated July 2026; separately assessed.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: AI-generated deception was used in a manner contrary to victims' informed economic choice. The OECD human-centred values principle is voluntary guidance; determining particular AI actor lifecycle duties remains a separate question, not a Dutch statutory verdict.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: Registered OECD AI Principles Section 1.2(a), 2024 voluntary guidance.

occurrence_environment.environment_detail: Scam operators used AI-generated recordings to reach real victims via live bank-impersonation calls.
occurrence_environment.evidence_basis: Police observed operational distribution of synthetic voice clips and downstream victim actions.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Synthetic bank identity supplied false economic solicitation and engineered trust cues that produced actual victim actions. Human-directed AI voice abuse qualifies without inventing autonomous criminal agency. Dutch police report card-data relay through a malicious app to accomplices making withdrawals. The relayed NFC material served payment authentication outside the legitimate cardholder–bank route. This is an attributed custody transition, not a claim that static public card identifiers alone are secret authenticators. Police reporting distinguishes synthetic voice generation, human call handling and separate card-relay and withdrawal actions; those roles do not reduce the fraud or losses.

primary_classification.classification_basis: AI-generated fake bank-security calls were material to inducing financial steps that enabled fraudulent withdrawals.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: Generated voices claimed bank authority and invented urgent risks as a distinct trust-inducing pathway.
False AI-origin bank urgency materially assisted scammers in eliciting actions victims did not choose on a truthful basis.

Dutch police report card-data relay through a malicious app to accomplices making withdrawals. The relayed NFC material served payment authentication outside the legitimate cardholder–bank route. This is an attributed custody transition, not a claim that static public card identifiers alone are secret authenticators.

Dutch police distinguish criminals’ AI-generated bank-impersonation clips, human operators’ scripted calls, and separate accomplices and software used for NFC relay and withdrawals. This bounded attribution is compatible with the harmful conduct and does not attribute independent criminal planning to an autonomous agent.
